reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.floor: the same steps written out by hand around the shipped writer and channel
reading.caveat: One rung of a ladder from a hand-written tracked write (`entity.title = value` after `===`, the entity queued once per frame) to `collection.updateEntity(slot, patch)`. Every rung writes the same slots of one population of priceDataset.batch entities, in the same loop, one { title } patch per round, and adds exactly one thing to the rung below it. Each pair re-measures the rung below as its floor in its own run, so a ratio prices only what its rung adds, and the rungs sum to the whole gap only to within the drift between runs. Up to the writer-object rung a frame is a hand-written stamp per entity and a queue, drained once per round; from the channel rung on it is the shipped channel and its flush. This rung adds: the collection running the same steps through its own methods and its own fields instead of the hand-written helpers and the hand-held object.

reading.floor: a subclass method doing only the one-channel path: assert, column-reader check, writer, channel, release
reading.caveat: Both sides run on a subclass of OIMEntityCollection built in the bench, over the same population of priceDataset.batch entities, one { title } patch per round and one flush per round; no index and no subscriber, so every write is one channel write. The subclass methods reach the same protected members updateEntity uses; only the shape of the door differs. This pair isolates: everything updateEntity carries beyond its one-channel path: the updatesEmptinessOnColumnWrite read and the branch into the subframe path.
